trust_decision.summary: Whether the SAML assertion that actually authorises the login is covered by a signature when the Response document element is not signed; decided in the broker by AssertionUtil.isSignedElement(decryptedAssertionElement) plus the 'any Signature node anywhere' test containsUnencryptedSignature, and in the servlet adapter by validateAssertionSignature()/validateResponseSignature() around the assertion taken from the response body.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('improper validation of encrypted SAML assertions') points at the broker login endpoint, where the assertion is decrypted at lines 559-582 and the signature decision is taken at 604-614; the flawed predicate containsUnencryptedSignature (line 607) is the first thing visible there.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP SAML identity-provider callback: GET/POST /realms/{realm}/broker/{alias}/endpoint and .../endpoint/clients/{client_id} (SAMLEndpoint.redirectBinding/postBinding/redirectBindingIdpInitiated/postBindingIdpInitiated, lines 174-227)
Deployed SAML servlet adapter callback (HttpFacade POST/GET to the protected application, via WebBrowserSsoAuthenticationHandler and EcpAuthenticationHandler)
Public library API AssertionUtil.decryptAssertion(ResponseType, DecryptionKeyLocator), called by both entry points above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the servlet adapter is a separate, client-deployed legacy library whose validateAssertionSignature is off by default (IDP.java:57-59), so the advisory about the Keycloak broker's encrypted-assertion validation does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Responses that carry a signature only on the assertion (response document element unsigned) must keep authenticating; requiring a document signature whenever an assertion is present or encrypted breaks assertion-only-signed IdPs.

O6_input_shapes: plain assertion child of Response (document-level or assertion-level signature)
EncryptedAssertion as the first assertion child of Response
assertion list where the encrypted entry and the plaintext entry are in either order (decryptAssertion now pins to index 0 instead of the first non-null encrypted entry)
assertion found by deep document search versus direct child of Response (new getAssertionElement)
post/redirect/artifact binding, each with a different notion of 'message fully signed'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The IdP-side SAML binding keeps its own containsUnencryptedSignature ('any Signature element') predicate and never got an isMessageFullySigned sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer applying the same 'fully signed' idea to client-supplied SAML messages would naturally copy the broker's abstract method into the protocol-side binding class.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The 'root not signed, so every Assertion must be signed' fallback ignores EncryptedAssertion elements entirely; a sibling that requires each EncryptedAssertion to be signed is a plausible hardening.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is exactly where the original authors put the assertion-completeness rule, and the encrypted case was simply forgotten.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second adapter profile (ECP/PAOS SOAP) that overrides the login-response handling with its own signature precondition.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adapter already ships two profiles over the same abstract handler, so a profile-specific duplicate of the check is a natural maintainer addition.

O9_family: SAML assertion signature validation bypass / authentication bypass (signature wrapping over encrypted assertions; CWE-347, CWE-1287)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module monorepo (maven.compiler.release=17); targeted modules build with `mvn -pl saml-core,services,adapters/saml/core -am`
O10_build.project_tests: Unit level: saml-core/src/test/java/org/keycloak/saml/processing/core/saml/v2/util/AssertionUtilTest.java and .../parsers/saml/SAMLParserTest.java; services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/saml/SamlEncryptionTest.java. End-to-end: testsuite/integration-arquillian tests/base/.../adapter/servlet/SamlSignatureTest.java (adds the new test) needs WildFly containers plus a browser harness, so it is heavy but offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Require the Response document element to carry a signature for every brokered/adapter login (or turn validateAssertionSignature on everywhere), which blocks the attack but breaks the legitimate assertion-only-signed IdP flow.

out_of_scope_notes: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/saml/SamlService.java:838-843 uses the same 'any Signature element' idiom, but that is Keycloak acting as the SAML IdP over client requests, not the assertion-login sink of this advisory; noted only, not pursued.
